title: Later exact gate entry overrides the first matching approximate entry
description: Ledger.gate uses share 0 whenever exact_native finds any exact entry, so a later exact entry beats the first entry with epsilon <= share (§8.3): wrong answer. Witness: two h, target entries [eps .001, time 1] then [eps 0, time 100], --epsilon 0.01: estimate gives time 200, error 0; §8.3 gives time 2 (share .005, first entry matches); bennett-sched gives 2. Reproduces at HEAD d32ef4f: test_e1_first_matching_approx_entry_precedes_later_exact_entry ('200' != '2'). Probe: bennett-estimate/.tmp/opus-reviews/probe/test_probe.py (runs src/estimate.py from the review worktree at d32ef4f); run: cd .tmp/opus-reviews/probe && python3 -W ignore -m unittest test_probe. Review: docs/reviews/2026-11-02-design-review.md (E1).
notes: Published pin e424d678 (unchanged SHA 021d5df...) explicitly fixes this in §17 item 9 / K58: an exact native match is tested before the accuracy filter, and gates with any exact native match take default share zero. The E1 request therefore normatively costs 200. New focused red/green coverage test_k58_exact_native_default_is_zero_but_explicit_share_keeps_array_order verifies default time 200/share 0, then explicit .005 shares select the first approximate entry and cost 2/error .002. That test passes. Changing the omitted-share result to 2 would violate the pinned published text. The review expectation needs correction; implementation defaults are retained. Full gate pending before closure.
close_reason: Adjudicated against pinned ISA 0.9 K58/17.9: any exact native match gets default share zero, so the omitted-share witness normatively costs 200. Regression verifies that answer and explicit-share first-entry cost 2. No contrary default implemented. Full scripts/pre-push --working-tree passes.
